prayerExcerpt.en-US: Be of stout heart, and fear not them who kill the body.
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: Tende o coração firme e não temais os que matam o corpo.

meta.face: A sturdy Anglo-Saxon man of about fifty with a broad, flat-planed, ruddy, weathered face, widest at the cheekbones, with a wide, blunt jaw; a short snub nose; small, clear blue, slightly hooded eyes; faint flaxen brows; a wide, straight mouth; fair flaxen hair cut short below the mitre, a short, square-trimmed flaxen beard flecked with grey, and a resolute, open gaze.
meta.basis: No portrait survives. The Fulda Sacramentary shows the sword-pierced book, the axe and the oak come from Willibald's Life, and later German images (Bloemaert, the Fulda statue) give him a beard. The flaxen colouring and the age at Geismar are choices to keep him off the white-bearded elder.
meta.excerpt: Willibald, Life of Saint Boniface, ch. 8, tr. G. W. Robinson (Harvard, 1916), his words to his companions at Dokkum (opening "Men and brethren," dropped); pt-BR our rendering
